# PLAN — iteration 5
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 0.148 ns register-to-register WNS, so iteration 5 must pass every deterministic gate and strictly improve that metric to become the new best. Iterations 2 and 4 did not improve it; iteration 3 lost timing closure after changing the state form. The supplied seed retains the transposed recurrence, and the baseline path excerpt shows a long DSP48 cascade, but that baseline evidence does not establish the seed’s routed metrics.

## Hypothesis
For the default coefficients, expressing the repeated constant products as signed shift-and-add logic may shorten DSP cascade paths and improve register-to-register slack while using fewer DSP48s.

## Instruction for generator
Keep `x_d`, `s0`–`s6`, `y_out`, their reset/update behavior, and `// @latency 1` unchanged. In the `p0`–`p7` product definitions, use exact 32-bit signed shift-and-add expressions when each corresponding parameter equals its default value (3, 7, 12, or 18); retain the general signed multiplication for overridden parameter values. Preserve the low 32-bit product and addition semantics, and compare routed register-to-register WNS against the 0.148 ns incumbent.
